note: Version 1. Anchors drafted by AI; student review is open. The worked examples are illustrative and invented to explain the levels: not real ideas, evidence or human labels, and not training data.
rules: available_hours = hours per week x weeks x team size, from the profile. compute_fit is true when the student's compute can build and run it. The hours gate itself is applied by the Verdict Engine.

anchors.0: Cannot be built: needs several times the available hours or compute the student cannot get.
anchors.1: Needs far more than the available hours, or major skills and compute are missing.
anchors.2: Needs somewhat more than the available hours, or a hard skill must be learned first.
anchors.3: Fits the hours with almost no margin, with some skills to learn.
anchors.4: Fits the hours with some margin; at most one modest skill to learn.
anchors.5: Fits the student's hours, skills and compute with margin: at most about two thirds of the available hours, no missing core skill.

input.idea: Train a large language model from scratch

evidence.summary: A report of the cluster and months such training needed.

expected.reason: Hours and compute far out of reach.

input.idea: A video editing suite for browsers

evidence.summary: A repository history showing years of work on a comparable editor.

input.idea: Mobile app with live sync, new to the team

expected.reason: Above the hours, with a hard skill to learn.

input.idea: Web app with sign-in and a small recommender

expected.reason: Margin of a quarter; one skill.

input.idea: Command line tool that checks README links

evidence.summary: Small comparable tools built by one or two people.

expected.reason: A third of the hours, known skills.
